item.title: Nonprofit organizations face unique operational challenges, but Google for Nonprofits is helping teams scale their impact faster than ever. Take The T...
item.description:
Nonprofit organizations face unique operational challenges, but Google for Nonprofits is helping teams scale their impact faster than ever.
Take The Tawaki Project in New Zealand: after adopting Google for Nonprofits, they transformed what would’ve been a 240-hour manual data transcription of their penguin research into a task that took mere minutes. This rapid data processing helped the team secure $1.1 million in funding and contributed to reclassifying the Fiordland crested penguin from “vulnerable” to “near threatened.” 🐧
On average, nonprofit participants in our Google for Nonprofits program report saving one full workday per person, per week on administrative tasks with AI. To support more organizations, we’re introducing new tools and resources on google.com/nonprofits, including:
• Practical, on-demand training courses focused on fundraising, marketing, and operations. • One-on-one productivity coaching with Google Product Specialists to guide technical migration and AI training. • Key industry insights detailing how 6,000 nonprofits are integrating AI into their daily operations to make the greatest impact.
Learn more → https://goo.gle/4vQK2Kn

item.title: "True technical leadership isn't about making tech more complicated — it’s about making sure nobody gets left behind," explains Sam, Google's Lead P...
item.description:
"True technical leadership isn't about making tech more complicated — it’s about making sure nobody gets left behind," explains Sam, Google's Lead Program Manager for AI Accessibility Research in Mountain View. Sam drives global roadmaps centered on clear, cross-team alignment.
In a role that impacts millions, his day kicks off with a critical huddle. "Upon arrival, my first priority is leading a briefing with my sign language interpreters," he says. "We use this dedicated time to map out the day’s logistics — ranging from high-level executive deep dives to granular technical sessions — to ensure seamless communication throughout every meeting.
Sam spends the rest of his day acting as a bridge between different teams — moving from executive pitch refinements and new hire mentoring to aligning engineering and legal cohorts on open-source AI accessibility guidelines. It’s a fast-paced choreography that shows complex technical roadmaps succeed when leaders focus on breaking down silos and keeping everyone moving in the same direction.
Want a closer look at his daily routine? Explore more of Sam’s career journey on our Careers site → https://goo.gle/4oCEDVA

item.title: We’re launching the first iteration of the AI & Economy ATLAS (Activity, Task, Landscape, and Adoption Study), the most comprehensive study to date o...
item.description:
We’re launching the first iteration of the AI & Economy ATLAS (Activity, Task, Landscape, and Adoption Study), the most comprehensive study to date on how people are actually using Google’s AI products and tools.
Based on 15 million de-identified interactions across more than 800 occupations, the data shows how people are using AI at work and at home:
💡 Collaboration over automation: At work, AI is primarily used for ideation and strategy, with less than 10% of interactions fully automating tasks. 🛠️ Beyond the desk: Workers in manual and technical trades are using AI as a live collaborator for real-time troubleshooting. 🏠 Everyday value: 86% of all AI interactions are happening outside of work, helping people navigate high-friction daily tasks. 🌍 Global growth: Global AI adoption is tracking GDP per capita, with exceptions. ATLAS data shows AI usage in 217 countries and territories that represent 99% of the world's population.
Learn more about our ATLAS report → https://goo.gle/4fhlbKX

item.title: "There's something magical that happens when you don't give up and learn to stay. Stay uncomfortable. Stay uncertain. The growth that awaits on the ot...
item.description:
"There's something magical that happens when you don't give up and learn to stay. Stay uncomfortable. Stay uncertain. The growth that awaits on the other side of that transforms you,” says Cristina, a Technical Program Manager on our Google Global Infrastructure (GGI) team.
Leaning into the unknown is exactly how she tackles some of our biggest scaling challenges. She oversees the operations, strategy, and budget to deploy our global physical network and high-performance TPUs (Tensor Processing Units—Google's custom AI chips designed to train massive machine learning models). Her core operating philosophy for managing these complex, fast-moving operations is incredibly simple: "Simplify, standardize, automate. In that order."
Cristina’s career advice for anyone navigating a new team or a big career pivot? Don't assume everyone else has the answers. Ask questions, embrace the learning curve, and don't be afraid to sit with the discomfort of growing.
Want to grow your career with Google? See what Technical Program Manager opportunities are waiting for you on the Cloud team → https://goo.gle/4pvBibb

item.title: Accurate weather forecasting saves lives and protects infrastructure, but predicting complex global atmospheric patterns requires immense computing po...
item.description:
Accurate weather forecasting saves lives and protects infrastructure, but predicting complex global atmospheric patterns requires immense computing power. NOAA: National Oceanic & Atmospheric Administration is taking a major leap forward by selecting Google Cloud as the primary provider of high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure for its Weather and Climate Operational Supercomputing System (WCOSS).
By transitioning to Google Cloud’s H4D virtual machines, NOAA becomes one of the first major global weather centers to move operational numerical weather prediction directly to the public cloud. This migration gives meteorologists and researchers unprecedented scale, speed, and AI capabilities to run massive simulations, refine prediction models, and issue faster, life-saving early warnings. Learn more from Google Public Sector. ⬇️A historic milestone for global weather forecasting. 🌤️
We are proud to announce that the NOAA: National Oceanic & Atmospheric Administration has selected Google Cloud as its primary HPC infrastructure provider—making it one of the first operational weather centers globally to move to the public cloud.
This marks the latest chapter in our long-term partnership to help NOAA protect lives and property nationwide. By combining Google Cloud’s secure, planet-scale HPC capabilities with NOAA’s unparalleled scientific expertise, we are helping ensure the United States remains at the absolute forefront of global weather prediction.
Read the full story here: https://goo.gle/4vVTjBc

On our Q2 2026 earnings call, Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai recapped an amazing quarter, with our AI investments redefining what’s possible across every part of our business. Learn more ⬇️Q2 was an amazing quarter, with our AI investments redefining what’s possible across every part of our business.
Alphabet revenue grew 24% YoY and Google Cloud accelerated to 82% growth. We saw exciting momentum across the board from Search to YouTube to the Gemini app (which reached 950M monthly active users). Our model APIs are processing 22B tokens/min (up from 16B+ last quarter) driven by our workhorse Flash models. We’re also seeing great adoption of Gemini Enterprise, used by 90% of the Fortune 100, as well as strong demand for our security solutions.
Outstanding results and momentum, and such an exciting moment—thanks to all of our partners and employees around the world! 🙌
